passages.note: House roll call 70 on third reading of HJR 3 lists Thompson among the Yeas, and the 57-40 split is far from near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: Section 38. Only a marriage between one (1) man and one (1) woman shall be valid or recognized as a marriage in Indiana.
passages.note: The enrolled resolution's single added constitutional section is the whole of its operative content; the only [deleted: ] fences on this page are in the printing-code legend, not in the provision.
The bill-details page shows HJR 3 is a single-subject measure ("Marriage"); Thompson is neither author nor co-author, so his act is the floor vote.

rows.reasoning: Thompson voted Yea on final (third reading) passage of HJR 3 (2014), a single-subject joint resolution whose entire operative content is "Only a marriage between one (1) man and one (1) woman shall be valid or recognized as a marriage in Indiana." That text both defines marriage as only between one man and one woman and denies same-sex marriages any validity, which is the rung reading "Make same-sex marriage illegal and define marriage as only between one man and one woman"; every other rung allows same-sex marriage or civil unions, and the resolution recognizes neither.
